stem: A coding agent's first attempt at a function fails two unit tests. Which TWO statements describe how reflection can help the agent on its next attempt? (Select TWO)

options.text: It can write a short lesson from the failing test output and keep it in context when it retries
It permanently updates the model's weights with a gradient step after each failed attempt
It guarantees that the next attempt passes every test
Critically examining the draft against the failing tests is a different task from generating it and can reveal the bug
It removes the need for any feedback about what went wrong

explanation.why_correct: Reflection helps in two ways here. Evaluating the draft against concrete evidence (the failing tests) is a different task from generating it, so it can surface the defect, and in Reflexion-style agents the resulting written lesson is stored and added to the context of the next attempt, which changes behavior without touching the weights.

why_incorrect.B: Reflexion-style learning happens through text carried in memory and context; the model's parameters stay fixed.
why_incorrect.C: Reflection improves the odds of a better attempt but guarantees nothing, particularly when the model misunderstands the requirement.
why_incorrect.E: Reflection works best when anchored to a concrete signal such as test results; without reliable feedback it may just restate the original mistake.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Reflection turns a concrete failure signal into a written lesson that the next attempt can use; it does not change weights and does not guarantee success.

stem: What role does a stopping condition play in a self-critique loop?

options.text: It eliminates the need for any critique step at all
It guarantees that the very first generated output is always already correct
It prevents the loop from running indefinitely once no further significant issues are found or a limit is reached
It forces the loop to run forever regardless of outcome

explanation.why_correct: A stopping condition halts the loop once the critique finds no further significant issues (or a max-iteration limit is hit), preventing unproductive extra rounds that would otherwise continue indefinitely.

why_incorrect.B: A stopping condition says nothing about the correctness of the very first output; it simply governs when to stop iterating.
why_incorrect.D: A stopping condition's entire purpose is to prevent the loop from running forever, the opposite of forcing indefinite continuation.
why_incorrect.A: The stopping condition depends on the critique step's findings; it doesn't eliminate the need for critique, it uses the critique's output to decide when to stop.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: A stopping condition is what prevents a self-critique loop from running unproductively forever -- it uses the critique's findings to decide when enough is enough.

stem: A self-critique loop's critique step is implemented in a way that always responds 'looks good, no issues' regardless of actual quality. What is the practical consequence?

options.text: The loop will faithfully catch and fix every error in the output
The loop provides essentially no benefit, since the overly lenient critique will approve flawed outputs without identifying real issues
The loop will run for an unnecessarily large number of iterations
The output quality will improve regardless of the critique's actual behavior

explanation.why_correct: Since the loop's value depends entirely on the critique step actually identifying real issues, a critique that always approves regardless of quality provides no meaningful improvement -- flawed outputs will simply be accepted immediately.

why_incorrect.A: An always-approving critique by definition never identifies issues, so it cannot catch or fix any errors.
why_incorrect.C: An always-approving critique would actually cause the loop to STOP immediately (since 'no issues' is a stopping signal), not run excessively long.
why_incorrect.D: Output quality will NOT improve if the critique never flags real problems; the loop's benefit is entirely contingent on the critique actually working.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: A self-critique loop's value is entirely dependent on the critique step genuinely identifying real issues -- a weak or overly lenient critique makes the whole loop ineffective.
